definitions.explanation: Medicine applied directly to the skin, such as ointments, creams, and lotions. Distinguished from oral or injected medications.

examples.japanese: {医者|いしゃ}に{塗|ぬ}り{薬|ぐすり}を{処方|しょほう}された。
examples.english: The doctor prescribed me a topical medicine.

examples.japanese: この{塗|ぬ}り{薬|ぐすり}は{一日|いちにち}に{三回|さんかい}、{患部|かんぶ}に{塗|ぬ}ってください。
examples.english: Please apply this ointment to the affected area three times a day.

notes:
USAGE:
A general term for any medication applied externally to the skin. Covers ointments, creams, gels, and lotions.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {塗|ぬ}り{薬|ぐすり}を{塗|ぬ}る (to apply ointment)
- {塗|ぬ}り{薬|ぐすり}を{処方|しょほう}する (to prescribe topical medicine)
- {塗|ぬ}り{薬|ぐすり}を{患部|かんぶ}に{付|つ}ける (to put ointment on the affected area)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {軟膏|なんこう}: ointment — more specific medical term for thick, greasy ointments
- {飲|の}み{薬|ぐすり}: oral medicine — medicine taken by mouth, the counterpart of {塗|ぬ}り{薬|ぐすり}
